So, lets take Ellie's run as the maximum of 5000 possible affinity points per run. To emphasize, this was only achieveable by stalling as long as possible, (a deeply unfun way to play), on the train event's hardest difficulty, and with a support affinity-farming Gramona.

Now, in order to reach affinity 10, you need 4500 points. That seems theoretically  achieveable in one run, but Ellie had fully built units, so i just want to temper any hopes newer players might have. Theoretically achieveable, but unrealistic to do so out of the gate.

Moving on, the affinity needed doubles to aff 11, with aff 15, you need 42000 points.

Aff 20 requires 168000 total.

In order to reach affinity level 20 from level 1, you need to do Madness Train stall runs 34 times. If you are doing it from affinity 10-20, you are going to do it 33 times. If you are doing it from 15-20, you need to do it 25.2 times. 

And ALL this, you can only focus on 3 units at a time, you need to have chaos in your team building, you fit gramona in that team, and you cant use auto battle.

Even her current critical damage scaling provides rapid diminishing returns, because her base damage numbers are EXTREMELY low, especially in the modern standards of the game. A single 280-300 damage hit, even multiplied by 400% simply isn’t even remotely enough to progress steadily through the normal story, let alone in endgame levels such as Phantasmal Dive or the DZone. 
If you’re wondering where the 280-300 number comes from, I did an extensive calculation table on various wheel equipment for Jenkins, found here: https://discord.com/channels/1131791637933199470/1170692781216378960/1541343906921451520
At the time of the data collection, I had a lv90 Jenkin at +12, with all “Gnostic Potential” levels unlocked. 

Jenkin is one of the first characters that players meet in the main story, and she’s one of the most unforgettable ones, first as the companion to Aigis, and then as our savior in the Wax Museum. With the game’s core concept of fighting against forgetting, shouldn’t you be caring more about characters like her?
Do not Forget: Jenkins

I feel like the best way to fix it without resorting to %HP would be to change the damage increase from flat %ATK to %-current-damage, or have it increase base damage by a % of base damage. So that as you keep using the attack, it scales faster and faster. It would still be comparatively slow, and would be balanced for both high level and low level content by default. But depending on how you play, that sort of (low-)exponential growth could be as effective as 24's scaling, I think? Or I'm talking out my ass lol. But like, increases base damage by 5% or 10% of current (/current base, but that would probably need higher scaling to work?) damage would feel a lot better to me, at least.
Its over, they aren't coming

We have identified that the Steam Deck currently does not fully support the display and signing functions required by our latest user agreement protocol. As resolving this compatibility issue involves complex verification and development time, we kindly ask for your understanding.

To ensure you can continue playing without interruption, please follow these steps:

Use an Alternative Device: Log in to your game account on a different device, such as a PC or Mobile device.
Sign the Latest Agreement: Complete the signing process for the latest user agreement on that device.
Return to Steam Deck: Once the agreement is signed, you may switch back to your Steam Deck to resume gameplay.
This workaround will allow you to bypass the current limitation on the Steam Deck while we work on a permanent fix. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your cooperation.

Could you please clarify whether your reinstallation was an "over-install" (installing over existing files) or a clean installation (uninstalling first, then reinstalling)?

To resolve the issue, please try one of the following methods:

Replace the Configuration File:
Contact a friend who plays Morimens and ask them to send you their _ab_info.json file, located in the Morimens\_game_data_\DownLoad\ directory. Replace your local version of this file with theirs, and then attempt to log in to the game again.

Perform a Clean Reinstallation:
Uninstall the game completely, ensuring no residual files remain. Specifically, verify that all files have been deleted from the following directories:

C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Morimens
[Your Steam Library Path]\steamapps\common\Morimens (if installed on a different drive)
Once these directories are completely empty, proceed to reinstall the game.
